name: Homestake chlorine detector

technology.value: Radiochemical chlorine detector: solar neutrinos capture on 37Cl to produce 37Ar via inverse beta decay in a large tank of perchloroethylene (dry-cleaning fluid), with the argon periodically extracted and counted
technology.quote: using the inverse beta-decay reaction to measure solar neutrinos ... extraction and counting efficiencies

placements.note: site:surf-surface-campus (owned by the fermilab-dune workstream; not created or edited here) is a `kind: campus`/`confidence: approximate` point for the whole SURF/Homestake site, used here per this workstream's brief as the fallback when no distinct sourced coordinate exists for the Davis chlorine-tank chamber specifically. This detector was actually ~1478 m (4850 ft) underground, NOT at the surface; the placement's role/time are sourced, but the site point itself only marks the general campus location, not the true underground depth -- flagged in `missing_fields`.

intervals.label: continuous operation
intervals.quote: The experiment operated continuously from 1970 until 1994.

target_mass.note: Wikipedia gives target volume (380 m3 / 100,000 gallons of perchloroethylene) but no source fetched this session converts this to a mass; left null rather than computed from an assumed density.

notes: Coordinate caveat: the site referenced (site:surf-surface-campus) is a surface campus point, not the detector's true ~1478 m underground location; see placement note.

summary.plain: A tank of dry-cleaning fluid, nearly a mile underground, that turned rare chlorine atoms into argon whenever a solar neutrino struck.
summary.technical: Radiochemical chlorine-argon detector, 380 m3 perchloroethylene target, 1478 m (4850 ft) underground in the Homestake mine; ran 1970-1994, measured 37Ar production rate 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU.
